items.title: Supreme Court seeks response from Goa on Tarun Tejpal's appeal against rape case conviction
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday issued notice to the State of Goa on a plea by former Tehelka editor Tarun Tejpal challenging his conviction in a 2013 rape case. A Bench of Justices MM Sundresh and PB Varale sought the state's response to the appeal filed by Tejpal against a Bombay High Court verdict convicting him and sentencing him to 10 years in jail. Pertinently, the bench also issued notice to Tejpal on an appeal filed by the State seeking enhancement of punishment from 10 years to life imprisonment. "Issue notice in both matters," the court directed. Senior Advocate Kapil Sibal , appearing for Tejpal, requested that the Court should refrain from issuing notice on State's appeal. He also prayed for a fixing a date for hearing Tejpal's bail plea. "Even the High Court suspended the sentence itself. Please fix a date for the bail as early as possible," Sibal said. "We will give a date. No problem," the Bench replied. items.title: Supreme Court lays down guidelines to check misuse of POCSO Act by parents in custody battles
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Thursday laid down nationwide safeguards to prevent the misuse of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act in matrimonial and custody disputes [ 'R' v. 'E' & Anr ]. A Bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and KV Viswanathan expressed alarm over the growing trend of warring spouses levelling false allegations of child sexual abuse against each other to gain tactical leverage in court. "Instances are not infrequent where gullible parties are misguided by their advisors, including in some cases by recalcitrant legal professionals, who in their pursuit of the motto of 'win at any cost', end up fuelling the fire...Very often, the enraged parent who is engulfed by anger and blinded by ego falls prey to these machinations, oblivious to the consequences that may ensue," the Court remarked. It said that such accusations inflict irreparable harm, public humiliation and unwarranted arrest on accused parents before they can establish their innocence. items.title: Allahabad High Court allows The Wire editor Siddharth Varadarajan to travel to US
items.summary: The Allahabad High Court on Thursday permitted The Wire founding editor Siddharth Varadarajan to travel to New York from September 28 to October 7. Justice Chandra Dhari Singh passed the order on September 23 after Varadarajan tendered an unconditional apology for not surrendering his passport as ordered by the Court in 2020. "This Court has also considered the fact that the applicant, present in Court, has tendered unconditional apology and has also given an undertaking to appear before the court concerned. The Court is of the view that, in the interest of justice, the apology deserves to be accepted. The delay/non-compliance for surrendering the passport, in terms of order dated 15.05.2020, is accordingly condoned," the Court ordered. It added that Varadarajan has been on anticipatory bail in the case since 2020 and the reason for his travel to New York appeared to be genuine. items.title: Full refund of court fee is legal entitlement when dispute is settled: Delhi High Court
items.summary: The Delhi High Court recently held that parties who amicably settle a suit, counterclaim or appeal are entitled to a full refund of the court fee paid and there is no need to file a separate application seeking refund [Hitech Enterprises v Modern Construction Company Delhi] . A Division Bench of Justices Anil Khsetarpal and Bharat Parashar observed that following an amendment to Section 16 of the Court Fees Act by the Delhi government, refund of court fee when the case is settled is a “substantive statutory entitlement”. “In view of the aforesaid, as and when, a matter is settled with or without invoking any modes referred to in Section 89 of CPC, the Court, while disposing of the matter in terms so arrived at, shall direct refund of the court fees. The Court shall also issue a certificate authorizing the parties to receive back full amount of court fees in respect of claim/counter-claim, thereby obviating the necessity of any obligations by parties to seek such refund,” the Court said.
